name: Tata Motors Ltd. (commercial vehicles; post-demerger)
business_summary: India's largest commercial vehicle maker (trucks, buses, vans, small CVs, e-buses) after the demerger that separated passenger vehicles into Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV). Promoter (Tata Sons) 42.5%. Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026): volumes 135,114 (+42.7%; domestic 113,982, international 21,132), revenue about Rs 25,300 cr per screener (+36%), OPM 10% (deck cites 11.7% on a different basis), PAT Rs 1,254 cr. Interest cost has fallen to ~Rs 100 cr a quarter. Strategic move: a public tender offer for Italy's Iveco Group at EUR 14.40 per share (~EUR 3.8-4 bn), which would double the scale and add a European CV platform; the offer crossed the acceptance threshold (HDFC Sky 2026-10-27) and a reopening window ran 2-6 Nov (search summary), with settlement pending regulatory steps. Segment splits are model estimates.

exposures.mechanism: CV is ~90% India-linked. +10% industry volumes -> TMCV revenue +8% (domestic share ~83% of volume) at ~20% incremental EBITDA margin vs 10% OPM -> EBITDA +16%; persistence 0.5; EV/MCap ~1.0 -> ~+8, haircut to 7 given H1 FY27 industry growth is already +24% (autocarpro) and the cycle is advanced.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 CV volumes 135,114 (+42.7%); domestic +30.9%; revenue +36%; PAT ~Rs 1,254 cr

exposures.mechanism: Roads, mining, construction and logistics capex drive M&HCV tippers and trucks. +10% capex growth -> volumes +4% -> EBITDA +8% -> persistence 0.5 -> ~+4.
Highway and road building lift tipper and HCV demand; +10% -> volumes +2.5% -> EBITDA +5% -> persistence 0.5 -> +2.5. Partly overlaps F_GOVT_CAPEX, so kept lower.
Freight volumes track GDP: +1 pp GDP -> CV volumes +3% -> EBITDA +6% -> persistence 0.6 -> ~+3.6.

Steel ~20% of costs (model estimate). +7% HRC -> costs +1.4% -> EBITDA -14% at 10% OPM; price hikes (CV price hike 2026-09-17, Upstox) recover ~50% with a lag -> -7%; persistence 0.3; EV/MCap 1.0 -> ~-2.1.
Aluminium ~3% of costs; +10% -> EBITDA -3%, half recovered, persistence 0.25 -> -0.4.
Tyres ~6% of costs, rubber ~40% of tyre cost; +10% -> costs +0.24% -> EBITDA -2.4% -> half recovered, persistence 0.25 -> -0.3.

Diesel is 50-60% of a fleet owner's operating cost; +10% Brent -> diesel +4% -> freight margin squeeze delays purchases; also raises plastics/paint costs. Brent +15% in 3 months but -5.6% in 1 month. The pack has no sensitivity table (new listing).

~90% of CVs are financed; +25 bp -> EMI +~0.7% -> volumes -1.5% -> EBITDA -3%, plus de-rating and TMCV's own acquisition financing; persistence 0.5 -> ~-1.5. Interest cost already fell from Rs 254 cr to Rs 100 cr per quarter.

International volumes +177% in Q2 (to 21,132 units) and exports ~15% of revenue vs ~10% imported content; +3% -> net +0.2% of revenue; EUR/INR exposure rises after Iveco closes (EUR-denominated debt and earnings).

After completion, Iveco's European truck/bus/van business (about the same EBITDA scale as TMCV's) makes European demand material: +1 pp EU GDP -> EU truck volumes +2.5% -> combined EBITDA +3.5% -> x completion probability 0.85 x persistence 0.5 -> +1.5.

evidence.note: Offer raised to EUR 14.40; acceptance threshold crossed; reopening window 2-6 Nov per search summary

exposures.mechanism: E-bus and e-truck demand (PM E-DRIVE, state tenders) with a Tata e-bus franchise; small revenue share, option value.
FIIs 19.0%; recently listed and index-eligible, supportive of flow-driven moves (e.g. +4% on 2026-10-27, up to +12% on 2026-11-05 sector rally).

Ashok Leyland, VECV (Eicher), Mahindra and BharatBenz compete in M&HCV and ILCV; Tata holds ~40% share (model). +1 unit = 2 pp share loss -> volumes -5% -> EBITDA -10% at 20% decremental margin -> persistence 0.5 -> -5.

supply_chain.note: Sister company from the demerger; shared brand and Tata Sons promoter; no ownership link
Pending acquisition via tender at EUR 14.40
Closest listed M&HCV rival; moves together on sector news (both up to 12% on 2026-11-05)

supply_chain.counterparty: Fleet operators / large logistics players, financiers (Tata Capital, banks)
supply_chain.note: CV financing availability is a demand driver

Iveco integration plan / squeeze-out and financing details; leverage rises
Union Budget: infrastructure outlay, scrappage and EV incentives
Q4 FY27 results and FY28 outlook

current_state.latest_quarter: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026, reported 2026-10-23): revenue ~Rs 25,338 cr (+36% per screener; Rs 23.9k cr in deck summary, basis differs), OPM 10% (11.7% per deck summary), PAT Rs 1,254 cr, FCF Rs 4.6k cr (deck). H1 volumes +35%.
current_state.trend: Strong upcycle: FY27 H1 industry volumes +24%; TMCV +35%. Margin down ~90 bp YoY on input costs and mix. Stock flat in 1 month, -5.7% in 3 months, then up to 12% on 2026-11-05 sector rally (reason not verified; one undated report links a similar spike to an Iran ceasefire).
current_state.valuation: P/E 22.4, P/B 10.4 (tiny book after demerger), mcap Rs 1.60 lakh cr; Nomura target Rs 511 (+29%, 2026-10-26).
